findings.description: Fixed by commit c980b1f and independently re-verified live by the release 0.1.0 security re-review (security-review.json reviewer_status APPROVED; SEC-1 not_required). WebhookAuthenticationFilter (IAsyncAuthorizationFilter, [TypeFilter] on ArrTagsWebhookController) authenticates before MVC model binding, fails closed with the uniform 401 for every content type, then rejects a non-JSON content type with a bounded 400 before any body read, so WebhookMaxPayloadBytes is the effective bound. Not an accepted limitation.

findings.description: SEC-2 accepted for V1 and now recorded in docs/limitations.md (RR-20 closed). When IPluginManager is unavailable or the loaded plugin instance cannot be found, CreateStateRepository roots authoritative state at Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "ArrTags"), a predictable shared location. Not triggered on the pinned host and not remotely reachable. Code re-verified this audit.
findings.recommended_action: Accepted for V1; optional post-V1 hardening to fail closed or use a host-private directory.

findings.description: SEC-3 accepted for V1 and now recorded in docs/limitations.md, with the reviewer-required wording correction applied. The versioned envelope SHA-256 (PayloadSha256) covers only PayloadJson; SchemaVersion is the only separately validated metadata field; Kind/RecordId/Authority are not validated by the envelope; Terminal/UpdatedUtc are trusted by retention. StateEnvelopeCodec is therefore a corruption detector, not a tamper MAC. Independently re-verified against the code this audit; the earlier overclaim phrase is absent.
evidence: docs/limitations.md:397-413 (corrected SEC-3 consequence); grep 'metadata tampering is detected' -> absent
src/ArrTags/State/StateEnvelopeCodec.cs:88 (hash compared against parsed.PayloadJson only), :144-149 (only SchemaVersion validated), :156-160 (SHA-256 over payloadJson only)
src/ArrTags/State/StateRepository.cs:77-82 (Read discards the parsed envelope, derives paths from caller arguments; Kind/RecordId/Authority not validated)
findings.recommended_action: Accepted for V1; optional post-V1 hardening to cover envelope metadata in the integrity hash.

findings.description: SEC-4 accepted and recorded; it is the already-recorded D1 gap (generic framework application/problem+json ProblemDetails body versus ADR-012's 'no body' wording). findings.recommended_action: Accepted for V1; optional post-V1 normalisation of error bodies / ADR-012 wording.

findings.description: SEC-5 accepted and recorded: API keys and the webhook secret persist only in Jellyfin's plugin configuration XML and are returned only by Jellyfin's authenticated, elevation-gated API (ADR-005 design). The plugin has no logging call sites. Independently re-checked this audit.
evidence: reproduced artifact scan: grep -ral for sonarrkey456|radarrkey123|webhooksecret789 -> no match

findings.description: SEC-6 accepted and recorded: it is the already-recorded D2 item (ArtworkSubjectGate.Gates has no idle eviction; not attacker-controllable and bounded in practice by distinct library items). No attacker-influenced unbounded collection was found.
findings.recommended_action: Accepted for V1; optional post-V1 idle eviction/LRU bound.

findings.area: webhook HTTP boundary / behavior change introduced by the SEC-1 fix
findings.description: SEC-7 accepted and recorded: after authentication a declared non-JSON content type is rejected with a bounded 400 before any read, so valid JSON sent with an unrelated content type is rejected. Absent content type is still treated as JSON; application/json, text/json, and +json are accepted. Sonarr/Radarr send application/json, so no real delivery is affected.
findings.recommended_action: Accepted for V1; documented behavior change.

findings.description: SEC-8 accepted and recorded: no ArrTags-level per-client auth throttling on the anonymous webhook route; mitigated by the high-entropy shared secret, the 1024-character candidate bound, constant-time compare, and uniform fail-closed 401. Optional post-V1 hardening only.
findings.recommended_action: Accepted for V1; optional post-V1 per-source throttling or reverse-proxy rate limiting.

limitations_accepted: F1 / RR-7 - No provider inventory/catalogue cache; provider metadata is fetched per work item. Consequence: a large library performs one provider-library read per work item, so GOALS criterion 6 is only partially met for provider fetches. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F1.
F2 / RR-8 - Runtime configuration replacement is not wired to Jellyfin's save path. Consequence: secret/provider/badge/limit changes require a process restart. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F2.
F3 / RR-9 - No bounded metrics/diagnostic-status surface. Consequence: no supported in-product view of queue depth/provider health. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F3.

F4 / RR-10 - Reconciliation coverage is bounded by QueueCapacity (default 512). Consequence: a scope larger than 512 covers only a bounded prefix per run; event/webhook/per-item triggers unaffected. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F4.

F5 - Renderer depends on a host-supplied SkiaSharp with no bundled fallback. Consequence: a host without a compatible SkiaSharp fails closed; validated only on the pinned linux-musl-x64 Jellyfin 12.0.0 host. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F5; ADR-015.
V1 - No live Sonarr/Radarr instance. Consequence: provider payload-shape variance beyond the committed fixtures is untested. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V1.
V2 / RR-11 - ADR-010 non-canonical cross-runtime comparison unselected/unrun. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V2.
V3 / RR-12 - Jellyfin Enhanced coexistence is contract-level only. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V3.
V4 / RR-13 - Automated live SaveImage read-back absent; the live round trip is manual. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V4.
V5 / RR-14 - Live uninstall drain: the release audit exercised it (204, install+state removed, artwork restored); automated coverage remains in-process. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V5.
V6 - Host-guarded facts are skipped without the pinned host. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V6.
P1 / RR-4 - Byte-reproducibility depends on the pinned toolchain and has no automated byte-identity guard. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P1.
P2 / RR-16 - Reduced debug metadata for reproducibility. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P2.
P3 - PackagePlugin=true stages but does not write the archive; ./build.sh package is the entry point. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P3.
P4 / RR-17 - SkiaSharp license notices ship although SkiaSharp is not redistributed. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P4.
P5 / RR-18 - Pre-release orphaned state/uninstall-drain retention. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P5.
D1 / RR-5 - Webhook 401 body differs from ADR-012's 'no body' text (generic ProblemDetails type/title/status/traceId). Evidence: docs/limitations.md D1.
D2 / RR-6 - ArtworkSubjectGate has no idle eviction. Evidence: docs/limitations.md D2.
RR-1 - Phases 1-3 lack independent phase-review records. Evidence: docs/limitations.md 'Release-review accepted limitations'.
RR-15 - Documented mock fixture API keys in tracked docs. Evidence: docs/limitations.md release-review section.

SEC-2 - State-root resolution falls back to a shared temp path when the plugin data folder cannot be resolved. Consequence: if the fallback engaged, authoritative state would live under /tmp/ArrTags; not triggered on the pinned host and not remotely reachable. Evidence: docs/limitations.md SEC-2; src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:178-180.

SEC-3 - The state-envelope integrity hash covers only PayloadJson, so StateEnvelopeCodec detects corruption but does not authenticate a malicious writer; retention trusts unauthenticated Terminal/UpdatedUtc. Consequence: none beyond the existing administrative boundary. Evidence: docs/limitations.md SEC-3; StateEnvelopeCodec.cs:83-113.

SEC-4 - Authentication error bodies carry framework application/problem+json detail (the recorded D1 gap). Consequence: a generic ProblemDetails body remains versus ADR-012's wording; no sensitive detail reflected. Evidence: docs/limitations.md SEC-4; D1.
SEC-5 - Secrets are stored at rest only in Jellyfin's plugin configuration XML. Consequence: none; accepted ADR-005 design with no plugin logging path. Evidence: docs/limitations.md SEC-5.

SEC-6 - The ArtworkSubjectGate process-lifetime bound (the recorded D2). Consequence: process-lifetime growth bounded by distinct library items and not attacker-controllable. Evidence: docs/limitations.md SEC-6; D2.

SEC-7 - A declared non-JSON content type is rejected with a bounded 400 after authentication. Consequence: valid JSON sent with an unrelated content type is rejected; Sonarr/Radarr send application/json, so no real delivery is affected. Evidence: docs/limitations.md SEC-7.

SEC-8 - No per-client authentication throttling on the anonymous webhook route. Consequence: optional post-V1 hardening only; mitigated by the high-entropy secret, candidate bound, constant-time compare, and uniform 401. Evidence: docs/limitations.md SEC-8; ADR-012.
